newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan gives central bank governor second term.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan gives central bank governor second term.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker government reappointed State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) governor Muhammad Yaqub for a second three-year term on Wednesday.

"He is a very competent person, the best person we have, and he will do exceedingly well," the prime minister's Finance and Economic Affairs Adviser Shahid Javed Burki told a news conference. "He's a hard-working, honest banker."
Burki, in charge of the finance ministry since President Farooq Leghari dismissed Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5, said Yaqub was respected in Pakistan and abroad.
Yaqub's second term begins on February 14, nine days after national and provincial elections set for Monday.
A U.S-trained economist and former International Monetary Fund official, Yaqub was named governor in July 1993 by then prime minister Nawaz Sharif on his last day in office.

He was retained by a three-month caretaker government led by Moeen Qureshi and then by Bhutto's three-year administration, despite initial controversy over a decree issued by Qureshi giving ground-breaking autonomy to the SBP.
In early 1994 Bhutto pushed a law through parliament that critics said watered down the bank's new-found autonomy, though the government denied that that was its intention.
Bankers and businessmen welcomed the news of a second term for Yaqub, an advocate of tight monetary and fiscal policy.
"The governor's reappointment is good for the banking system and economy. He believes in transparency," Muslim Commercial Bank vice-president Maqsood Ahmad said.
"The banking industry, which was in a very bad shape, needs him. We hope he will restructure the whole banking system and put it on a sound footing."
Kalim Aziz, an analyst at Baring Securities, said Yaqub's continued presence would have a positive impact on banks.
"He believes in independence and transparency. The recent restructuring of the banking system has been done on the initiative of Dr Yaqub," he told Reuters.
Karachi Stock Exchange president Arif Habib praised Yaqub as "a supporter of the capital market".
Younas Khan, country chief of Deutsche Bank in Pakistan, said Yaqub was "the right man for the right job".

Burki and Yaqub have worked together to craft a series of financial sector reforms aimed at stopping the rot in state-run banks which have racked up huge portfolios of non-performing loans under politically-appointed management teams.
They have also designed measures to strengthen the central bank's role in formulating and enforcing monetary policy and in regulating and supervising the banking sector.
